claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2. nodes.md: "Marking a node as unschedulable prevents the scheduler from placing new pods onto that Node but does not affect existing Pods on the Node." Note: "Pods that are part of a DaemonSet tolerate being run on an unschedulable Node." §3 now carries the exception ("except Pods that run one per node") and §4 "apart from the ones that run on every node". Lab drain.txt lines 1-11.

kubectl drain reference: "The given node will be marked unschedulable to prevent new pods from arriving. 'drain' evicts the pods if the API server supports ... eviction"; it names the owners it accepts: "replication controller, replica set, daemon set, stateful set, or job". disruptions.md: "When you run `kubectl drain`, the tool tries to evict all of the Pods on the Node". Lab drain.txt lines 23-32.

Carried from round 1, claim unchanged. api-eviction.md: "`429 Too Many Requests`: the eviction is not currently allowed because of the configured PodDisruptionBudget." disruptions.md: "deleting deployments or pods bypasses Pod Disruption Budgets."

Carried from round 1. kubectl drain reference: "If there are daemon set-managed pods, drain will not proceed without --ignore-daemonsets ... then drain will not delete any pods unless you use --force." --delete-emptydir-data: "Continue even if there are pods using emptyDir". drain.txt lines 13-16 list all three refusals, the first with "cannot delete cannot delete".

kubectl drain reference: "those pods would be immediately replaced by the daemon set controller, which ignores unschedulable markings." drain.txt line 15 lists kube-system/kindnet-... among "DaemonSet-managed Pods". "kind's CNI plugin" rests on the claim ledger of k8s.l3.cni-plugins (not re-verified here, unchanged from that lesson). Round 3: §4 rewording (kindnet in parentheses) changes no meaning.

Carried from round 1. volumes.md: "When a Pod is removed from a node for any reason, the data in the `emptyDir` is deleted permanently." kubectl drain --force: "Continue even if there are pods that do not declare a controller."

Carried from round 1. configure-pdb.md: "`.spec.selector` ... This field is required." "You can specify only one of `maxUnavailable` and `minAvailable` in a single `PodDisruptionBudget`." web-pdb.yaml uses apiVersion policy/v1.

Round 3. configure-pdb.md: healthy = "`.status.conditions` item with `type="Ready"` and `status="True"`. These pods are tracked via `.status.currentHealthy`". probes.md line 205: "If a container does not provide a particular probe, the kubelet always considers the result as `Success`." So with no probe, running containers count as ready. maxUnavailable 1 on 3: "the exact same meaning"; minAvailable = replicas: "zero voluntary evictions".

disruptions.md: "the tool periodically retries all failed requests until all Pods on the target node are terminated, or until a configurable timeout is reached." kubectl drain --timeout: "The length of time to wait before giving up, zero means infinite". §6 and summary line 4 now name `--timeout` and the no-timeout case. drain.txt lines 27, 48.

Round 3: claim 10 and §6 now use the round-2 suggested_text. disruptions.md: "Involuntary disruptions cannot be prevented by PDBs; however they do count against the budget." configure-pdb.md: a node may fail "when the collection is at the minimum size specified in the budget", leaving none allowed; with slack, fewer remain allowed. "allows fewer evictions, or none" covers both cases.

Carried from round 1. disruptions.md: "deleting deployments or pods bypasses Pod Disruption Budgets." drain.txt lines 58-59: "pod \"<a web Pod>\" deleted from lifecycle-lessons namespace" right after the 3-of-3 drain timed out.

Carried from round 1. kubectl drain --pod-selector: "Label selector to filter pods on the node". drain.txt: plain drain refused (lines 13-16), drain with --pod-selector=app=web on the same node ends "node/donhang-worker drained" (line 32).

debug-service.md: "The label \"app\" is automatically set by `kubectl create deployment` to the name of the Deployment." scripts/lib/network-lessons.sh line 5: show() { echo "\$ $*"; "$@"; }. drain.sh line 18: pods() lists POD, STATUS (.status.phase), NODE; line 20: drain() pipes through awk '!seen[$0]++' (each line once).

persistent-volumes.md: "Pods that use a PV will only be scheduled to nodes that are selected by the node affinity." local-path-provisioner README (WebFetch, round 1): PVs use "the `kubernetes.io/hostname` label for node affinity". drain.sh lines 83-95: Deployment store, replicas: 1, no PodDisruptionBudget for app=store. drain.txt lines 61-72.

Carried from round 1. Conditional recommendation ("If the application must keep serving during maintenance"), follows from claim 14 and disruptions.md: "Replicate your application if you need higher availability."

Round 3: §5 sentence now equals the round-2 suggested_text. drain.sh lines 59-62: delete web Pods on donhang-worker2 (--wait=false), cordon donhang-worker2, rollout status, uncordon. drain.txt lines 44-50: the strict drain evicts two web Pods and lists two pending, so two of three were on donhang-worker. The web-pdb drain (lines 22-36) ends "node/donhang-worker drained".
